# Plate Reconstruction — Design and Reference

## Design Principle

The pipeline is reconstruction-agnostic. All plate-model-dependent paths flow from `plate_model_name` and `use_provided_plate_model` in the config. Adding a new reconstruction requires only populating `data/{name}/` and writing a config file — no code changes.

## How Reconstruction Loading Works

`lib/plate_models.py` provides two main functions:

- `get_plate_reconstruction(model_name, model_dir, ...)` — if `use_provided_plate_model: True`, scans `model_dir` for `.gpml`/`.gpmlz`/`.rot` files; otherwise fetches via `PlateModelManager` with a local-file fallback. Returns a `PlateReconstruction` object.
- `get_plot_topologies(...)` — same model resolution; additionally resolves coastlines, continents, and COBs. Returns a `PlotTopologies` object.

Both accept a `filter_topologies` flag which removes inactive deforming networks and flat-slab topologies via `lib/misc.py::filter_topological_features()`. When enabled, a temporary file handle is returned alongside the object to prevent garbage collection.

`lib/setup_run.py::run_setup()` (invoked via `python run_notebooks.py --setup --config <file>`) handles directory creation and either triggers a PMM fetch or validates the provided model files before any notebooks run.

## Reconstruction-Specific Files

For PMM-fetched models, all layers are downloaded automatically. For provided models, place files under `data/{plate_model_name}/plate_model/`; all `.rot` and `.gpml`/`.gpmlz` files in the directory are loaded recursively.

Files resolved by name pattern for provided models:

| Layer | Pattern matched |
|---|---|
| Static polygons | filename contains `static` + `polygon` |
| Coastlines | filename contains `coast` |
| Continents | filename contains `continent`, `terrane`, or `static` + `polygon` |
| COBs | returned as `None` for provided models |

## Source Raster Provenance

All rasters are generated by `00a-generate_data.ipynb`. Citations from Alfonso et al. (2024), *GSA Bulletin* v. 137.

| Raster | Source | Reconstruction-dependent? |
|---|---|---|
| Seafloor age | Williams et al. (2021), *Geoscience Frontiers* | **Yes** |
| Seafloor spreading rate | Derived from seafloor age | **Yes** |
| Silicic sediment thickness | Dutkiewicz et al. (2019), *Geology* | **Yes** — polynomial coefficients may need re-fitting; see [#10](https://github.com/MaxEtherington/PUB-framework-Alfonso/issues/10) |
| Carbonate sediment thickness | Dutkiewicz et al. (2017), *G-cubed* | **Yes** |
| Sediment pore water volume | Athy (1930), *AAPG Bulletin* | **Yes** (derived from sediment rasters) |
| CO2 in upper oceanic crust | Müller & Dutkiewicz (2018), *Science Advances* | **Yes** |
| Crustal thickness | Cao et al. (2017), *Biogeosciences* (Matthews2016 paleotopography) | **Yes** |
| Erosion/deposition | `lib/erodep/` | **Yes** |
| Magnetic anomaly | EMAG2v3, Meyer et al. (2017), NOAA NCEI | **No** — static present-day grid; single copy at `data/shared/EMAG2v3/` |

## Adding a New Reconstruction

1. Populate `data/{name}/plate_model/` with model files, or set `use_provided_plate_model: False` to let PMM fetch them.
2. Write `config/run_baseline_{name}.yml` with the correct `plate_model_name`.
3. Run `python run_notebooks.py --setup --config config/run_baseline_{name}.yml` to validate and prepare directories.
4. Run `00a` to generate rasters.
